newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chile denies contact with Canadian sailor - reports.
newsitem.headline: Chile denies contact with Canadian sailor - reports.

text.p: The Chilean military has denied that a boat in radio contact with a rescue plane near Cape Horn 10 days ago had identified itself as the yacht of missing Canadian sailor Gerry Roufs, French media said on Saturday.
The reports said the skipper of the unidentified boat only replied "Go ahead" -- in English with a French accent -- when asked if it was Roufs' Groupe LG2. Then contact was lost.

French radio and newspaper correspondents in the southern Chilean town of Punta Arenas quoted the local Chilean Navy commander Jorge Minoletti Olivares as saying the brief radio contact took place on January 16 at 1030 a.m. local time.
The commander said another plane searched the area later in the day and found nothing.
Chile had earlier reported a plane had made radio contact with a boat which identified itself as "Groupe LG".

Later air and sea searches by the Chilean and Argentine navies failed to spot Roufs who has been out of touch since early January when he was sailing in a remote Antarctic area between New Zealand and Chile.
Roufs is competing in the French-organised Vendee Globe Challenge, a solo round-the-world race.
The race's organisers and the French maritime rescue service which is coordinating the search for Roufs said they were trying to get the latest reports confirmed by Chilean authorities.
Two other competitors in the race, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore, were rescued by the Australian navy after their boats capsized southwest of Australia.
